newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weaker on dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weaker on dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened for a second consecutive day against the dollar on Tuesday as demand for dollars outstripped supply, commercial bank dealers said.
"There is a lot of demand coming in from oil importers, and we're seeing very little supply from coffee and tea exporters who normally are in the market by Tuesday," a dealer told Reuters.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.44 against the dollar from 55.01 on Monday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at 89.86 from 88.08.
Dealers said panic dollar-buying, triggered by the shilling's drop below 55 against the dollar on Monday, pushed the shilling down to touch 56 before the central bank intervened to help the currency.
"If the central bank had not intervened, we would definitely be trading past 57 against the dollar by now," one dealer said.
Commercial bank dealers said the shilling, which ended strong last year, was likely to continue its downtrend until demand for food import costs hit the market.
"A famine disaster is long term, and the shilling will continue weakening for as long as it prevails," a dealer said.
The money market was liquid with many banks lending. Overnight rates were quoted below 10 percent levels, unchanged from Monday.
